issue.title: Router data should always be available to children components

**Current behavior**
If a route with an empty path shares data to its children, the data is inherited and we can access the data from the resolver and the data of the route, but, if we have a route with a path, the children don't have access to the route data nor its params.

It looks like the data is being consumed by the parents. So the parent can see the data, but its children cannot.

To better understand what I mean, please look at the plunkers provided in the issue.

**Expected behavior**
The parent component should not consume the data, so that its children can get the same data.

http://plnkr.co/edit/zpmMLC?p=preview

body:
It seems to me that we can use ActivatedRouteSnapshot freely inside 'resolve' method of Resolver or when ngOnInit is called. But when we subscribe on data changes then we have a transition state of route inside a handler. Maybe this state is before the route becomes completed IMHO. 
It needs clarification also when and where we can use snapshot. Maybe it is a bug.
That's interesting. Is there any documentation of order when those events occur?

@klinki None that I could find. You might want to open an issue about that over at the [angular.io](https://github.com/angular/angular.io/issues) repository if you feel like this should be documented.

issue.title: ActivatedRoute order of actions

repository.name: angular.io
repository.description: Website for the Angular project (see github.com/angular/angular for the project repo)

issue.body:
It would be nice to have some documentation of order of actions on ActivatedRoute.

By actions I mean:
- When Observables receive new data
- When Navigation events occurs
- When ActivatedRouteSnapshot is updated
- When other route parameters get updated

And possibly more interesting actions. See https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/12912 for motivation for this.

body:
This really seems strange to me. We resolve data,  activated routes route.params and route.data are both updated with new data in the component - but the route is still not active. In my case I wanted to navigate further based on the data, and made the mistake of doing relative navigation when processing route.data. Resulting routes were relative to the old route, resolver wasn't called again on the resulting new routes, and everything was just generally messed up.
I think documentation should really highlight that when processing activatedRoute.data might not be the best time to actually update your component (unlike the example at https://angular.io/docs/ts/latest/guide/router.html#!#resolve-guard) since the route is not actually activated yet. (Of course if you wait for navigation end you lose much of the advantage of resolve as the component may then flash as it updates.... You cant win with the current design.)
Looks like a bug in `advanceActivatedRoute()` where the snapshot is assigned at the end. Needs more investigation

Finally I've found out that `routeReuseStrategy.shouldReuseRoute` always returns `true`. In the  function two configs (future and current) are compared, but they are always the same. There is no way to substitute `ReuseStrategy` via `ExtraOptions` for now, but in future version maybe.
This is what I dont like from angular to other SPA, different version, different buil-in function/syntac. Everything change and then new bug waiting for solution again.

@skreborn The `event instanceof NavigationEnd` doesn't work when user refreshes the page - I find myself having to merge two streams: router.events and activatedRoute.url - and do some clever filtering to prevent the function I want to run from firing maaaany times. Quite annoying.
